$comment: Yesan full-scale test site (Zenodo 21441974). NOT SCORING READY.
TWO FRAMES PER LINE, deliberately kept apart. 'yesan:testbed-A/B' is the CONSTRUCTED testbed, from the
Korea Expressway Corporation design report EXTRI-2018-40-534.9607: its targets are authoritative for where
objects were built (grade B: positions read off the design figures). 'yesan:line-A/B' is the authors' 2021
radar distance convention. Nothing registers one to the other: the 2021 direction, start alignment and the
27 m / 3116-interval calibration are unresolved, so every target is in the testbed frame only and the
scoring gate stays shut. No offset is guessed and no radar feature is used to place a target.
Targets are generated from evidence/yesan/kec_testbed_targets.csv by scripts/build_yesan_manifest_targets.py.

exhaustive.statement: Not attested. KEC Tables 4.6 and 4.8 reconcile exactly with the drawn objects (asphalt 40, concrete 42), but the approach-slab section does not (drawn 34, table rows 36, text 38: two steel plates unaccounted for); 5 moisture sensors drawn in the asphalt section are instrumentation outside the tables; and nothing establishes that the 2021 site held exactly these objects.

frames.origin: the authors' '0 m reference position', given per file as a trace number in 'summary of GPR data and formula.xlsx' (file 66: trace 65; 72: 96; 69: 107). What physical marker it is, is not documented in the held files.
frames.registration_note: Two distance scales disagree: the .rad wheel calibration gives 0.008429 m/trace (line A stops at 90.70-91.05 m) while the authors' sheet uses dx = 0.0086649550706 m/trace (93.23-93.59 m), about 2.8% longer and roughly 2.5 m over the line. Which one the target chainages use is unknown. The per-file 0 m trace (65/96/107) is where the authors put 0 m; its relation to the targets' chainage origin is unproven. The KEC design (testbed frame yesan:testbed-A) is NOT registered to this frame: the 2021 direction, which trace is above testbed 0 m, and which scale (if either) equals testbed metres are all unresolved.

depth_reference_surfaces.description: top of the road pavement along the line. KEC: the shallowest cavity model sits 'directly beneath the pavement' at 0.27 m, the thickness of the asphalt layers (5+7+15 cm); the concrete minimum 0.45 m is the 30 cm slab + 15 cm lean base (PDF pp. 82-86, 113). Rhee et al. 2021 states the EPS depths are to the object's top surface.

open_questions.statement: RESOLVED FOR THE TESTBED (2026-10-05): the constructed objects are listed in KEC report EXTRI-2018-40-534.9607 Tables 4.6-4.8 and placed in Figs. 4.5/4.7/4.10; transcribed in evidence/yesan/. Whether the 2021 site held these objects is yesan-site-identity; which trace is above which object is yesan-testbed-to-2021-registration.

The testbed origin is now declared (start of the asphalt section; a buried steel plate on line B, none on line A). Still unproven: that each 2021 file's '0 m reference position' trace (A: 65/96/107; B: 80/60/60) lies over that origin.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors, or a site drawing tying the 0 m marker to the target positions

open_questions.statement: The .rad interval 0.008429 m is 3 pulses / 355.9 pulses per metre; the authors' dx = 0.0086649550706 m equals 27/3116 (to 1e-13), i.e. a 27 m reference spanning 3116 trace intervals, 2.8% longer. The KEC report (90 m site, three 30 m sections) contains no 27 m calibration distance and cannot explain it. Which scale, if either, equals testbed metres is unknown.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors: which distance calibration the published target chainages use

open_questions.statement: KEC design landmarks: abutment stem 44.7-45.3 m, footing 44.0-46.0 m; approach-slab/concrete boundary 60 m; plain/CRCP boundary 75 m. The 2021 near-surface changes (44.0-45.0, ~60, 72.6-75.6 m) coincide with all three if sheet 0 m ~ testbed 0 m, which now favours the shared-chainage hypothesis over a 14.5 m offset. This is a consistency check, NOT a registration, and is not used to place anything.

Every .rad header reads 'ANTENNAS:500 MHz shielded'. The folders say 250/500/800 MHz, and the evidence supports the folders: SIGNAL POSITION falls into three groups that coincide with the folder labels, and the recorded spectra have centroids of ~270, ~450 and ~715 MHz in the 250/500/800 folders. Inferred, not confirmed.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors; until then a frequency breakdown must cite the folder label, not the header

open_questions.statement: QDM repetition files name the same sections at other distances (approach slab_A_11-15 m, reinforced concrete_A_26-30 m, ascon_B_0-5 m), so at least two unstated distance conventions are in use.

Inferred, not declared: the landmark coincidences hold only if both 2021 lines start at the asphalt end (a reversed run would put the 60 m and 75 m changes at 30 m and 15 m). The authors have not stated the direction.

That the Zenodo 21441974 site IS the KEC testbed is inferred (same operator, same 90 m bridge-transition layout, QDM names on KEC chainages, radar changes at KEC landmarks) but not stated by any held source; the report anonymises the site. Objects may also have changed between construction (2017-18) and the 2021 survey.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors (Oh, Chang-Geun) or the dataset's MDPI Sensors paper

open_questions.statement: No defensible transformation maps a 2021 trace to testbed chainage: it needs the survey direction, the trace over testbed 0 m on each line, and the meaning of the 27/3116 calibration. Target positions are known; which trace is above them is not.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors; not to be fitted from radar features

open_questions.statement: KEC gives depths below the pavement surface but does not say to which point of a non-EPS object (top, centre); Rhee 2021 states top for EPS only. The transverse drain's 1.5 m may be its centre (the drawn box top is ~1.05 m).

KEC and Rhee 2021 figures disagree for 26 of 74 compared objects (|delta| > 0.15 m): concrete line-A depths 0.2-0.4 m apart, concrete drain/hemisphere 4.6 vs 5.0 m, start plate 0.26 vs 0.46 m, end plate 29.74 vs 29.40 m. Kept explicit in evidence/yesan/rhee2021_vs_kec_comparison.csv; KEC is used, not adjusted.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors, or the as-built GPS coordinates (KEC Table 4.22)
